hook: An outcast boy of the steppe who built the largest land empire in history.

pages.x: Temujin was born around 1162 by the Onon River in Mongolia. Legend says he came into the world clutching a blood clot in his fist, a sign that he would be a great leader. When he was nine, his father, a chief, was poisoned by enemies.

His father's clan abandoned his mother and her children to the wilderness. They survived on roots, fish and marmots. As a teenager Temujin killed his half-brother in a fight over food, and was captured by enemies, but escaped from the wooden collar they locked on his neck.

Through war and alliances he united the feuding tribes of the steppe, and in 1206 a great gathering named him Genghis Khan, "universal ruler". He organised his army in units of ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand, and promoted men for loyalty and skill, not birth.

His horsemen conquered northern China, taking Beijing in 1215, then the Khwarazmian Empire in Central Asia, whose governor had killed his merchants and envoys. Cities that resisted, like Bukhara, Samarkand and Merv, were destroyed and their people slaughtered.
pages.img: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire

pages.x: He set up the Yam, a chain of relay stations a day's ride apart, where messengers found fresh horses, food and rest.
pages.fx: News could travel 300 km a day across Asia. With safe roads and religious freedom, the revived Silk Road carried goods and ideas between China and Europe.

pages.x: He died in 1227 during a campaign in China, perhaps after a fall from his horse. Legend says his funeral escort killed everyone they met on the way, and that horsemen trampled the grave flat so no one would ever find it. No one has.

Genghis Khan's empire, under his sons and grandsons, stretched from Korea to Hungary. He was a ruthless destroyer, but in Mongolia he is the father of the nation, and millions of people alive today may descend from him.
pts: Founded the largest land empire in history
